name: Southwestern Tarahumara
readall_conflicts: No source describing the Southwestern Tarahumara [twr] variety itself was opened, so no direct conflict exists. Two indirect signals pull different ways and are noted for the record: (a) Villalpando 2010 (held by the project, MA thesis on Turuachi; p. 27, quoting the CET 1992 dialect survey) states 'Posición del acento: Este rasgo delimita una zona OESTE que se comporta distinta en función del acento, el cual recae sobre la vocal final en la variedad OESTE, mientras que recae en la penúltima para las otras variedades' (Tabla 9: makói 'ten', sikúi 'ant' in Norte/Centro/Cumbre/Sur vs makué, sikuí in Oeste) — i.e. penultimate in the Sur area, which Caballero 2022 Table 1.2 (p. 7) and Villalpando 2010 Cuadro 2 (p. 15) equate with Ethnologue's Southwestern [twr]; but Ethnologue's own twr entry is the Tubares-area variety, not INALI's Sur (Turuachi/Chinatú), so this mapping is uncertain. (b) Caballero 2022 for Choguita (Central [tar]) describes lexically contrastive, weight-insensitive stress within an initial three-syllable window plus lexical tone. Neither statement is about twr proper; the survey's three-word 'penultimate' feature is a dialect-differentiating diagnostic, not a stress rule.

sources.citation: Caballero, Gabriela. 2022. A grammar of Choguita Rarámuri (Comprehensive Grammar Library 5). Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7189161. 687 pp.

sources.note: Describes Choguita Rarámuri, which the author places in Ethnologue's Central Tarahumara [tar] (p. 6: 'Choguita Rarámuri is part of the Alta Tarahumara dialect continuum within a "Central" dialect area within the Ethnologue's classification ([tar]; Eberhard et al. 2021)'), i.e. glottocode cent2131, not sout2971. Ch. 5 Stress (pp. 133-164): lexical stress with minimal pairs (p. 134: ˈmúri 'basket' vs muˈrí 'turtle'); p. 135: 'There is no evidence for secondary stress in Choguita Rarámuri.. Stress is left-aligned and assigned in the first (2a), second (2b–c) or third (2d–e) syllable of the word.…

sources.note: §2.3 Fonología (pp. 45-49): consonant inventory of Cuitaboca Tarahumara (17 consonants, Tabla 5-6 with example words), 5 vowels without length, free alternations t~ɾ, ɾ~l, e~i; explicitly defers deeper phonology to Caballero 2008 and Villalpando 2010. No sentence on stress/accent placement; transcriptions carry IPA stress marks (e.g. [pa.na.ˈla] 'cara', [be.ˈbe.ki] 'tierra', [to.to.ˈli] 'gallina', [mu.ˈki] 'mujer', [pe.ˈle.ta.ɾa.li] 'semana', [wa.ka.ˈsi] 'vaca', [ˈjo.la] 'enojo') = wordlist-level stress data only, varying position within the first three syllables.

Nothing on stress. Establishes identity: alt. names Tarahumara del Suroeste, Tubare; 100 speakers (1983 SIL); location 'Chihuahua state: Tubare'; status 8a moribund; 'Typology: Nontonal'; unwritten; 'Area where extinct Tubare [tbu] language was spoken'. The tcu entry (capture 2019-12-15) carries the names 'Balleza, Chinatú, Rarámari raicha, Tarahumara de Chinatú, Tarahumara del Sur, Tarahumara del Sureste', so INALI's 'Sur' (Turuachi/Chinatú) is tcu, not twr.
